introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, answer all questions): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Why is it necessary to use a gel where the ultrasonic probe is placed?

(ii) State, with respect to medical diagnosis, one advantage that

- X-rays imaging has over ultrasound imaging

- ultrasound imaging has over X-ray *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Why a gel is needed.** Air between the probe and the skin would **reflect almost all the ultrasound** (the acoustic impedances of air and of soft tissue are very different, so more than 99 % of the energy would be reflected at the air-skin boundary). The gel has an acoustic impedance close to that of the skin, so it **excludes the air**, gives good contact and ensures that the ultrasound is **transmitted into the body** (impedance matching).

**(ii) One advantage of each** (any one in each case):

- **X-ray imaging over ultrasound:** X-rays give a **sharper image of dense structures** such as bones (greater resolution and contrast of bone), and they can pass through air-filled organs (lungs) and bone to image the interior, where ultrasound is reflected or absorbed.
- **Ultrasound imaging over X-ray:** ultrasound is **non-ionising, so safer** (it can be used on a foetus and repeated often); it shows **soft tissue** boundaries clearly, gives **real-time moving images**, and the equipment is cheaper and portable.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Describe the changes that occur to a human eye when the eye changes from focusing a distant object to focusing a near one, both objects being [...] viewed under bright light.

(ii) A patient's eye is said to be astigmatic. State the effect of astigmatism on the image produced by the defective eye, its cause and the shape of the lens used for correction.

A patient's near point is located $210\ \mathrm{cm}$ from his eyes.

(iii) What type of eye defect is the patient suffering from?

(iv) Use diagrams to explain the type of lens needed to correct this defect so that the patient should be able to read a book placed $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ from his eyes. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Accommodation (distant to near).** The **ciliary muscles contract**, the **suspensory ligaments slacken**, and the elastic **lens becomes thicker (more curved)**: its focal length decreases and its power increases, so that the image of the near object is formed on the retina (the image distance, lens to retina, stays the same). The eyes also **converge** (turn inwards) towards the near object. Because both objects are viewed in the same bright light, the pupil stays small and its size does not change the focusing.

**(ii) Astigmatism.**

- **Effect:** the image is **blurred or distorted**: lines in one direction (for example vertical) are in focus while lines in the perpendicular direction are not, because the eye has different focal lengths in different planes.
- **Cause:** the **cornea (or the lens) is not spherical**: its curvature is different in different planes (like the surface of a rugby ball).
- **Correction:** a **cylindrical lens** (curved in one plane only, with its axis set at the proper angle) which adds the missing power in the weak plane.

**(iii) Defect.** The near point (210 cm) is far beyond the normal 25 cm: the patient is **long-sighted (hypermetropia)**; close objects cannot be focused on the retina (the eyeball is too short or the lens too weak).

**(iv) Correction with a converging lens (diagrams described).**

- *Diagram 1, uncorrected eye:* rays from a point of the book at $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ diverge strongly; the weak eye lens would bring them to a focus **behind the retina**, so the image on the retina is blurred.
- *Diagram 2, corrected eye:* a **convex (converging) lens** in front of the eye makes these rays less divergent, as if they came from a **virtual image** of the book at $210\ \mathrm{cm}$, the patient's near point; the eye can focus this on the retina.

Focal length: object distance $u = 25\ \mathrm{cm}$ and virtual image distance $v = -210\ \mathrm{cm}$ (real-is-positive convention):
$$\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{25} - \frac{1}{210} = 0.0352\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}\;\Rightarrow\; f = 28.4\ \mathrm{cm}$$
**A converging lens of focal length about $28\ \mathrm{cm}$ (power $\approx +3.5\ \mathrm{D}$) is needed.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Figure 15* shows the electrocardiogram waveform obtained at the surface of the skin of a patient.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_11_fig_1.png)

From the ECG waveform, determine the pulse rate per minute. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each heartbeat produces one sharp (QRS) peak. From figure 15, the first peak is at $t \approx 0.25\ \mathrm{s}$ and the next one at $t \approx 0.95\ \mathrm{s}$, so the **time for one beat (period)** is
$$T = 0.95 - 0.25 = 0.70\ \mathrm{s}$$
$$\text{pulse rate} = \frac{60\ \mathrm{s\,min^{-1}}}{0.70\ \mathrm{s\,beat^{-1}}} = 85.7\ \text{beats per minute}$$
**Pulse rate $\approx 86$ beats per minute** (acceptable reading: 85 to 87).
